messages:
tina: quick postmortem follow-up: we saw token TTLs written in ms vs s during the DB migration. this caused thousands of tokens to live far longer than intended. need owners for remediation, an audit, and a short runbook.

harold: i'll take the runtime fix. plan: normalize all TTL writes to seconds in the library boundary, add validation that rejects TTLs outside 10s-30d, and gate behind `AUTH_TTL_VALIDATE` flag. aiming for PR by 2026-04-01.

maya: i'll run the audit and build alerts. initial script: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "auth:token:*" | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c 't=$(redis-cli ttl {}); if [ "$t" -le 10 -o "$t" -gt 2592000 ]; then echo {},$t; fi'` — will optimize for scale and post CSV. target audit done by 2026-03-28.

ops-oncall: prepping a condensed rotate playbook: 1) export CSV, 2) group by service, 3) if >1500 tokens -> automated rotate with 24h grace, else manual rotates, 4) enable strict flag in canary 10% for 2h, 5) validate audit logs for each rotated token, 6) store proof artifact. scheduling a 30m prep call tomorrow.

harold: added CI test `ci/ttl-writes` that asserts writer library sets TTL in seconds. will include an integration test that simulates mixed binaries.

maya: audit found ~1.7k anomalies across 2 services, csv uploaded to SEC-5102. will triage with service owners for targeted rotates.

tina: owners and due dates: HAROLD (runtime PR + tests) due 2026-04-01; MAYA (audit + CSV + alerts) due 2026-03-28; OPS-ONCALL (runbook + prep call) prep call 2026-03-27. please update SEC-5102 as you make progress.

sec-bot: SEC-5102 status updated 7: follow-ups assigned (automated).

tina: final note 0 add one-liner to runbook: "TTL must be written in seconds (s) across all writer binaries" and include the redis audit snippet. mark done in ticket when added. thanks everyone.
